Classify a pedon in the FAO-Unesco soil legend

Source: R/key-fao.R
classify_fao.Rd

Keys a PedonRecord through the FAO-Unesco legend of the Soil Map of the World. Experimental: this release keys the 28 major soil groupings of the Revised Legend (FAO 1988, World Soil Resources Report 60; the text of the ISRIC reprint of 1997, Technical Paper 20), chapter X, pp. 75-89, and their 153 soil units, in the key's order (Histosols, Anthrosols, Leptosols, Vertisols, Fluvisols, Solonchaks, Gleysols, Andosols, Arenosols, Regosols, Podzols, Plinthosols, Ferralsols, Planosols, Solonetz, Greyzems, Chernozems, Kastanozems, Phaeozems, Podzoluvisols, Gypsisols, Calcisols, Nitisols, Alisols, Acrisols, Luvisols, Lixisols, Cambisols), on the 16 diagnostic horizons and 27 diagnostic properties of chapters IV and V read on the data. Under its grouping a soil keys to the first soil unit whose gate passes, in the key's order; the last unit of each grouping is the key's "Other ..." residual (Haplic, Eutric, and the Terric Histosols and Urbic Anthrosols, whose descriptions are shown, not tested). Since v0.9.386 the result also gives the 16 phases of chapter VIII (pp. 67-71) and the texture and slope classes of the map symbol (Appendix 2, p. 107) in $phases, beside the unit, which they never change. Since v0.9.389, edition = "1974" keys the Legend of 1974 (FAO-Unesco, Soil Map of the World, Vol. I, Unesco Paris), pp. 43-53: its 26 major soil groups in the key's order (Histosols, Lithosols, Vertisols, Fluvisols, Solonchaks, Gleysols, Andosols, Arenosols, Regosols, Rankers, Rendzinas, Podzols, Ferralsols, Planosols, Solonetz, Greyzems, Chernozems, Kastanozems, Phaeozems, Podzoluvisols, Xerosols, Yermosols, Nitosols, Acrisols, Luvisols, Cambisols) and their 106 soil units (the Lithosols, Rankers and Rendzinas are single units), on the diagnostic horizons and properties of 1974 read on the data; its registry id is fao1974 (classify_fao1974). Since v0.9.390 its result gives in $phases the 12 phases of 1974 (pp. 5-7: stony, lithic, petric, petrocalcic, petrogypsic, petroferric, phreatic, fragipan, duripan, saline, sodic, cerrado) and the texture and slope classes of its map symbol (pp. 4-5), in the same form.

Usage

classify_fao(
  pedon,
  edition = c("1988", "1974"),
  rules = NULL,
  on_missing = c("warn", "silent", "error"),
  gapfill = FALSE
)

Arguments

pedon

A PedonRecord.

edition

"1988" (the Revised Legend, default) or "1974" (the Legend of 1974).

rules

Optional pre-loaded rule set (load_rules("fao1988"), or load_rules("fao1974") with edition = "1974").

on_missing

One of "warn" (default), "silent", "error".

gapfill

Opt-in within-pedon gap-fill, as in classify_usda.

Value

A ClassificationResult with system_id "fao1988" ("fao1974" for the Legend of 1974); name holds the soil unit as printed ("Haplic Luvisols") and rsg_or_order the major soil grouping ("Luvisols"); levels has one row per level (major_groups, units) with the code ("LV", "LVh"), name, page of the key and soilKey's Portuguese gloss (name_pt); the key trace of both levels and provisional_because; and phases, a data.frame with one row per phase and one per class of the map symbol (kind "phase", "texture_class", "slope_class"), its status ("present", "absent", "undecided", or "not shown" for a unit the text excludes), present and criterion (TRUE, FALSE, NA), page, basis, flags and the attributes that would decide an undecided phase (missing).

Details

The tests are three-valued: a measurement not recorded leaves its criterion undecided, a field observation not recorded is absent. A grouping or unit tested before the assigned one that the data leave undecided makes the result provisional (provisional_because, "major_groups:<code>" or "units:<code>": the candidates). The key has no residual grouping after the Cambisols: a soil that no gate takes is "[Not classified in the FAO-Unesco Revised Legend (1988)]", in brackets because the name is soilKey's, with the gates that failed in the warnings; when no gate passes but some are undecided, the name lists them in brackets as the candidates. Depths are read from the soil surface, H and O horizons included. The readings where the text is silent are in system.file("rules", "fao1988", "readings.yaml", package = "soilKey").

References

FAO (1988). FAO/Unesco Soil Map of the World, Revised Legend, with corrections and updates. World Soil Resources Report 60, FAO, Rome. Reprinted with updates as Technical Paper 20, ISRIC, Wageningen, 1997.

See also

classify_fao1988, classify_fao1974, make_fao_example, soilkey_systems.

Examples

res <- classify_fao(make_fao_example("LV"), on_missing = "silent")
res$name
#> [1] "Albic Luvisols"
res$rsg_or_order
#> [1] "Luvisols"
res$levels
#>          level code           name                             name_pt page
#> 1 major_groups   LV       Luvisols               Luvissolos (Luvisols)   88
#> 2        units  LVa Albic Luvisols Luvissolos Álbicos (Albic Luvisols)   88
res$phases[res$phases$status != "absent", c("kind", "code", "name", "status")]
#>             kind     code            name    status
#> 6          phase  inundic   Inundic phase undecided
#> 9          phase phreatic  Phreatic phase undecided
#> 17 texture_class        2 Medium textured   present
#> 18   slope_class     <NA>            <NA> undecided
classify_fao(make_fao_example("Lc", edition = "1974"), edition = "1974",
             on_missing = "silent")$name
#> [1] "Chromic Luvisols"
